thread:
ana: heads-up — we got a customer (fintech) hitting cross-region latency issues when we fall back to variant-b. they want deterministic tier routing by region and a softer degrade path.

david: can you paste a short example of the request flow? is this the hosted API path or dedicated?

ana: hosted API. traffic starts in eu-west, primary model = redwood-7b-v1, fallback = redwood-quant-7b. problem is when primary fails we send to us-east and latency spikes.

sasha: oh, so routing_by_region is falling through to remote region because capacity policy picks cheapest compatible zone. we currently do: region_probe -> availability -> capacity_score -> pick. no explicit latency bound.

jin: idea: add latency_threshold_ms per customer tier + per-route region_affinity window. e.g. for enterprise tier, prefer same-region unless estimated p50 + probing_penalty < threshold.

kelsey: +1. Also need to record telemetry when we route off-region for SLA billing and debug. i.e. emit metric: routed_region != client_region with tags {customer_tier, model_variant, fallback_reason}.

mike: agree. also want a graceful fallback chain: same-region compatible quantized variant -> same-region different instance pool -> nearby region (eu-central) -> remote region (us-east). avoid last-resort unless capacity emergency.

ana: here's a proposed minimal config we can surface in console for 'Region routing policy':
```json
{
  "policy_name": "region_affinity_v2",
  "tiers": {
    "enterprise": { "latency_threshold_ms": 120, "region_affinity": "strong", "fallback_order": ["same-region-compatible","same-region-burst","nearby-region","global"] },
    "standard":   { "latency_threshold_ms": 250, "region_affinity": "preferred", "fallback_order": ["same-region-compatible","nearby-region","global"] }
  },
  "probe_weight_ms": 80,
  "penalty_on_probe_fail": 150
}
```

jin: UX thought: console should show for each customer the active policy, recent routed_region samples (sparkline), and % of requests that hit fallback variants. we should surface a button: "simulate route" where SREs can run a sample request to see where it would go.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: routing-service/config v1.14 -> canary on infra-us-east-2 at 2026-03-05T15:30:00Z

ana: telemetry hooks: add two histograms: routing_latency_estimate_ms (when selecting) and actual_request_latency_ms (post-response) both labeled by customer_tier, client_region, routed_region, model_variant. also increment counter fallback_triggered{reason}.

david: how do we prevent oscillation? e.g., probe says eu-west healthy but quickly degrades and we flip back and forth between eu-west and eu-central.

sasha: add hysteresis with cooldown window per source-ip/prefix and use EWMA probe history. also penalize region_score for short-term failures. we already have circuit-breaker state per region-model tuple. make sure tie-breaker prefers stability.

kelsey: for billing correctness, if we route off-region for > 5% of requests in a 1h window we should notify account owner and auto-open support ticket. data exportable to CSV from console.

mike: edge case: model variant compatibility. if primary is fp16-only and same-region only has quantized variant, we need to decide: prefer identical semantics (fp16 remote) vs approximate semantics (quantized same-region). product wants semantic parity for enterprise. config needs a 'semantic_priority' flag.

ana: good call. add flag example: "semantic_priority": "prefer_same_semantics" vs "prefer_same_region".

jin: internal API: Suggest augmenting RouteDecision proto with fields: chosen_region, fallback_chain[], probe_scores[], decision_reason string. that helps debugging from traces.

ops-bot: trace created: trace_id=tr-9a8b7c route_decision dump attached to request 0x4f2d.

ana: rollout plan: 1) add metrics + RouteDecision proto change behind flag, 2) add console UI for policy editing + simulation (beta), 3) run canary for 24h for 10 enterprise accounts, 4) widen out.

david: dependencies: routing-service, probe-agent, console, billing-notifier, trace-exporter. assign owners?

sasha: i'll own probe-agent & routing-service changes. jin will own console UX and simulation. kelsey owns telemetry and billing-notifier hooks. mike will design fallback semantics. ana will coordinate rollout and write runbook.

kelsey: runbook checklist: how to force route to specific region for mitigation, how to revoke canary, how to escalate. add screenshot examples for console button paths.

ana: quick hack discussion: could we do a temporary per-customer override via API? yes, create PATCH /v1/customers/{id}/routing_override {"force_region":"eu-west"} with TTL. ops only.

mike: small question: do we store per-customer policy in global db or regional control plane? storing globally simplifies editing but increases risk — if control plane in us-east flaps, editing might be slow. suggest replicated config with consistent versioning.

sasha: prefer replicated config (push to region control planes) with version numbers; routing-service checks version and falls back to builtin default if missing.

ana: OK action items: 
- sasha: implement latency_threshold and cooldown + probe EWMA (ETA 4d)
- jin: console simulation prototype + UI mockups (ETA 7d)
- kelsey: add metrics + billing notifier rule (ETA 3d)
- mike: define semantic_priority options and add to config schema (ETA 2d)
- ana: write canary plan and runbook (ETA 2d)

mike: can we get a quick perf estimate for the extra probe_score telemetry? shouldn't be much. sasha?

sasha: tiny overhead (RPC + 2 tags), negligible compared to inference cost.

ana: thanks all — i'll open tracking ticket and put links in the canary invite. :rocket:

jin: nice. i'll post the console mocks here once ready.

ops-bot: canary started: routing-service v1.14 canary -> infra-eu-west-1 (10% enterprise), started at 2026-03-06T02:10:00Z
